fact: A Topline Research Solutions survey found mobile money leading digital platforms at 52 percent adoption in Zimbabwe.
ZimSwitch's chief executive described it as the national payment switch, with mobile wallet integration on its e-commerce platform and interoperable QR payments being rolled out.
Equity Axis says EcoCash, O-Mari, Innbucks and NetOne One Wallet operate as mobile money platforms in Zimbabwe.
Equity Axis says O-Mari wallet holders withdraw cash at CABS ATMs and EcoCash customers at TN CyberTech Bank ATMs, and that ZIPIT allows some cross-platform transfers already.

The Herald quotes the RBZ governor saying all mobile money operators' wallets were rescreened against the Civil Registry by 30 June 2026, and that mobile banking apps, mobile money platforms and QR payments are growing in use.
The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe reported about 208.8 million mobile-money transactions worth ZiG76.2 billion in the first quarter of 2026, around 87 per cent of electronic-payment volumes.
The World Bank report says mobile money is used by 63 percent of Zimbabwe's population and mobile and internet payments exceed 80 percent of retail transaction volumes.
The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe asked banks, mobile money operators and other digital payment providers to eliminate ghost accounts, indicating mobile money operators are in service.
RBZ reports 11,246,479 active mobile money subscribers at 30 June 2026 and mobile money transactions of ZiG94.9 billion in Q2 2026.
Per the article, ZIPIT and mobile money are in use, EcoCash is accepted through Paynow, and the RBZ raised their per-transaction limit from ZiG 8,000 to ZiG 13,000 in February 2026.
The RBZ raised mobile money and ZIPIT transaction limits to ZiG13,000 per transaction from ZiG8,000, person to person or business, with a ZiG50,000 monthly cap.
The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe reports mobile money carried 206,575,490 transactions, 86.70% of volume and 10.51% of value, in Q4 2025, with 10.96 million active mobile financial services subscribers.
TechAfrica News says mobile money services in Zimbabwe continue to thrive, with millions of citizens and businesses using digital wallets and mobile platforms for daily transactions.
Business Times reports ZB Financial Holdings launched Smile Cash, an in-house mobile wallet usable by app or USSD, and the Smile&Pay merchant gateway, at about US$250,000 investment.
NewsDay describes EcoCash as Zimbabwe's largest fintech platform whose customers can now send money abroad directly from their EcoCash wallet to bank accounts or mobile wallets.
Econet Wireless Zimbabwe describes an EcoCash wallet in use, with an agent network and cash-out, reachable by dialling *153#.
POTRAZ director-general Gift Machengete said about 11 million people, roughly 70% of the population, use mobile money in Zimbabwe.
